feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany continued its slow recovery from its record low
entry.summary: Germany's main shipping gauge read 20 centimetres on 13 October, up from 17 centimetres the day before. — Sources: Kaub gauge readings, direct fetch via rivercruise.ai, 13 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fire-hotspot count swung up and down well past its 8 October peak
entry.summary: The Ministry of Forestry recorded 11,772 hotspots nationally on 10 October, well below the 20,818 already reported for 12 October, showing the count rose again after an earlier, sharper dip from its 24,952 peak on 8 October. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Forestry, via databoks.katadata.co.id, 8-12 October 2026

entry.title: Singapore's air stayed in the unhealthy band through 10 October
entry.summary: The 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index reached 176 in central Singapore at 7am on 10 October, the most recent confirmed reading, with other regions ranging from 125 to 162 the same morning as haze from Indonesian fires continued to drift across the region. — Sources: The Star Malaysia, 10 October 2026

entry.title: UK and European mortality surveillance both read back at their expected baseline
entry.summary: The UK's health security agency found no signal of mortality above the expected baseline for the week of 8-14 September. — Sources: UK Health Security Agency, Weekly all-cause mortality surveillance, week 41 2026 report (week 37 data) · EuroMOMO Bulletin, week 32 2026
